group.note: Category column, one ridge per level. Blank = the first non-numeric column.

value.note: Numeric column whose distribution is drawn. Blank = the first numeric column.

overlap.note: How far each ridge rides over the one below. 0 separates them completely.

scale.note: peak normalizes every ridge to the same height, so shapes compare but a group of 5 looks as tall as one of 5000. common keeps one density scale, so height means something.

median_line.note: Mark each group's median inside its ridge.

add_count.note: Weld n= to each ridge label — with peak scaling this is the only cue to group size.

order.note: Pin named groups first; the rest stay ordered by descending median.

catalog.name: Selom Ridge Plot
catalog.summary: Stacked kernel-density curves, one per group — the distribution-shape companion to box and violin. Shows what a five-number summary hides: two separated modes and one broad spread produce near-identical boxes but obviously different ridges. Discloses its own smoothing bandwidth, and names any group excluded for having too few values to estimate a density from.
